messages:
alex: Heads-up: I ran into an ops snag tonight while testing manifest rotation. The proxy cache expired and some requests failed because the control plane was flaky. We need an offline-friendly spec for tenant manifests.
maya: Ugh. Did the proxy try to fetch the full manifest or just validate a sig?
alex: It tried to fetch the full blob after seeing a manifest-id header. Control plane had a short blip so fetch timed out and we returned 503s for a subset of tenants.
sam: We should ensure proxies can make safe routing decisions with only a signed header (manifest id + sig + a couple of effective fields). Full blob fetch should be optional.
jing: Agreed. Proposal: split the surface into two layers: (A) a tiny routing header with canonical fields that the proxy can always evaluate offline (signed, ~200B max), (B) a larger manifest stored in registry for observability and admin UI.
maya: What fields are "canonical"? we want to avoid leaking sensitive config but still make correct routing choices.
sam: Minimum: tenant_id, manifest_id, latency_profile, sensitive_data_flag, eviction_tier, model_fallback_hash. Signed with current key-id and sig.
alex: Also add an expiry timestamp and key-id so proxies can reject very old headers and know which signing key to validate against. For private deploys the signature check might use a local trust bundle.
jing: Signature rotation question: when we rotate signing keys, old headers must remain valid until expiry. But proxies may have a cached trust bundle. We need an explicit key-rotation handshake: publish new key, start signing with new key, keep old key in trust bundle for N hours. Ops needs a recommended rotation window.
maya: We should default to a 24h overlap window and make it configurable per-deploy. Private customers can set their own rotation policy.
sam: Another failure mode: manifest-id collision or reuse across tenants. Manifest ids must be globally unique (CID-like) and never recycled within retention window. We'll document generation rules.
alex: Good call. Also, runtime overrides: if an operator applies a runtime override via API, how does proxy see that? We currently write an ephemeral override object in registry that proxies poll. But for offline mode, runtime override should also be emittable as a signed short header by the gateway to avoid missing it during fetch outage.
jing: That raises an auth question: who can sign overrides? Only control plane keys. Allowing gateways to sign means they need private key material or a pre-signed token issued by control plane. Better: control plane issues short-lived override tokens (JWT) that gateways attach. Proxies validate token signature + token audience.
maya: We should provide example header form. Something like:

X-RW-Tenant: t-abc123
X-RW-Manifest-Id: mf-2026-03-21-xyz
X-RW-Manifest-Sig: sig-v1:KID:BASE64
X-RW-Manifest-Expiry: 1700000000
X-RW-Override-Token: eyJhbGciOiJS...

sam: And a compact JSON payload that fits into a single header for embedded manifests (for private bundles):
{"tenant_id":"t-abc123","latency_profile":"low","sensitive":false,"eviction":"tier1"}

alex: We must keep header size <= 512 bytes for older proxies. If unsigned embedded manifests exceed that, proxies should fall back to fetching local bundle file.
jing: For private deployments: manifest bundle is deployed with the control plane package and lives in /etc/redwood/tenant-manifests/<tenant>.json. The proxy must first look there, then check header signature only if bundle absent. Documented priority: local bundle > signed header > registry fetch.
maya: Telemetry: every routing decision must emit manifest_id and effective_routing_source (local-bundle|header|registry) so we can audit and debug mismatches.
sam: Testing: we need a conformance test harness for proxies that validates signature verification, expiry handling, rotation overlap, offline heuristics, and fallback ordering. Could be a small harness in go that mocks control plane and asserts behavior.
alex: Ops concern: eviction semantics across modes. Dedicated clusters may have stricter eviction tiers. Proposal: eviction_tier maps to a cluster-local priority number; proxies consult a cluster policy file to turn eviction_tier into numeric weight. This keeps tenant manifest stable across modes while letting cluster ops tune mappings.
jing: Edge case: a tenant marked sensitive but with fallback list that includes hosted-only models. Proxy must block fallback across private boundary. So manifest must include an explicit "allowed_hosting_modes" array, default to [hosted,dedicated,private].
maya: Action items: alex write a 1-pager with header spec + size constraints + priority mapping; sam prototype a small proxy conformance test harness; jing capture private bundle filesystem layout and trust-bundle rotation mechanics; ops-bot: add infra task to include key-rotation runbook.
ops-bot: Task created: infra/manifest-offline-spec, link: https://go/infra/manifest-offline-spec (assigned). :spiral_calendar:
maya: We'll reconvene after prototypes. If anyone hits an outage repro, post logs to #eng-sre with timestamps.
alex: Thanks all.
